commit.message:
Show execution-host Codex usage on the iOS voice screen (#12016)

The Talk with Codex list gains a Codex account usage section: the account,
plan, quota windows with percentages and resets, and the last-updated time
for the computer that handles the call. It reads the existing
ListAgentAccounts RPC (the same AgentAccountsSnapshot the CLI reads, #12022)
with the desktop's cadence: a cached read, then a forced probe at most every
30 s per computer, and a 5 min poll. A live call keeps its own computer even
if next-call preferences change; replies from an earlier computer are
dropped. No computer, offline, sign-in, unsupported and failed refreshes are
stated as such, and missing data never shows as 0%.

Rust (client_ffi/voice_usage.rs) owns host selection and state; UIKit only
presents it. Swift bindings regenerated with build-core.sh.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add the #12019 on-device check to After-close checks

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show Working while a saved account chat answers on iOS (#12019)

The saved account transcript now sets the shared Working row from the
Turns snapshot's busy flag, the same flag behind Stop. It shows before
answer text arrives and clears when the answer finishes, stops, fails, or
observation pauses, and after a chat or account switch. Builds on
02dd4ce52a (the adapter and layout tests) and adds one guard so a shut-down
history view never shows Working.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Phone: no way into the demo for people, and no demo exit chip or row

The demo stays for the Design Lab screenshot tour, which starts it with
-demo. The welcome screens lose "See a demo", and the exit chip strip and
Settings row from #12011 go, since nobody can be in the demo but the tour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read Codex account quota from the CLI with explicit freshness (#12022)

`openagents accounts usage --device local|UUID [--harness codex]
[--account active|ID] --json [--refresh] [--ipc-port PORT]` reads the
running app engine's shared usage cache through the existing
ListAgentAccounts RPC. Output carries cachedAt/usageFetchedAt, ageMs,
state (fresh/stale/neverFetched/unavailable), a stale flag, usage and
refresh errors kept apart from last-good windows, and refresh results
of updated/cached/failed. No RPC or DTO shape change; openagents-rpc
drops its sync dependency's default SQLite store so the root CLI links.

Builds on the earlier unfinished session's work in the old worktree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix current runtime settings in SDK agent turns (#12018)

Bind the settings chosen for the turn into the existing SDK runner input. Keep identity edits pinned to the assigned revision and cover runner changes and native-to-SDK changes with the public runner contract.

Start the identity with the device name after leaving the demo, and regenerate the phone's Swift bindings (#12011, #11995)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix the desktop identity tests' local deployment address (#11997)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Answer an app's refusal of a read with a signed refusal (#12000)

When the app's dispatcher refused an app RPC, the host returned through
`?` out of execute, so the device got no signed reply and waited out its
timeout; DeviceChannel then saw a transport failure (Unavailable) where
it expects `unsupported`, and never fell back. LinkAccount on a computer
without an account key hit this in the engine's pairing test.

Now a refused read, and a definite refusal of an effect (unsupported,
malformed, bounds, forbidden, missing right), earns a signed refusal. An
effect whose outcome is unknown still gets no reply, so a retry asks
again and the command ledger keeps it to one run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

SDK docs: plain words for two modules, the known unlinked calls listed, the reference regenerated (#12007)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Regenerate the SDK reference, app and Computers contracts; read generated request types in the reference; list the sign-in routes as non-screens (#12007, #12001)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add a way out of the phone's offline demo (#12011)

The demo had no way back to the real app. A "Demo · Exit" chip now sits
in a strip at the top of the shell while the demo runs, and Settings
shows an "Exit demo" row in place of Sign Out. Both stop the demo
client, remove its data folder, and start this phone's own account the
way a launch does, without restarting the app.

The Rust core owns the words (`demo_exit_copy`, checked by the oa-copy
guard) and `forget_demo_data`, which removes only a folder named `demo`.
Rust tests cover exiting a demo client and keeping the account's folder.

Nothing from the demo reaches the account any more: the demo gets its
own cloud chat and own-computer record instead of the account's, keeps
its new-session page in memory, and "See a demo" sets a signed-in
account aside instead of signing it out. A UI test enters the demo and
leaves it from the chip and from Settings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add the desktop app to Design Lab (#12010)

Design Lab now holds two apps, Phone and Desktop. Desktop capture runs
sit in the captures folder's desktop/ folder; each app's newest run
decides which of its screens are current, desktop screens are filed as
desktop:<area>--<screen> with pictures under desktop/, and the board
gets a Phone / Desktop switcher (P, #app=desktop) that draws desktop
frames at their own aspect ratio and starts mocks at the app's size.

The desktop tour (crates/ui/src/shell/design_lab_tour.rs, behind
account-fixture) opens the whole shell offscreen in a 1280 x 800 point
window with fixture data and a loopback fixture account, and saves the
boot gates, Home, the sidebar, a chat with tool rows and its menus, the
right-pane panels and every Settings page in light and dark mode. The
design-lab-tour example and scripts/design-lab-capture-desktop.sh run it.
GPUI keeps element bounds private, so desktop shots have no element trees.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add the SDK docs at /docs/sdk, generated from the contracts and the SDK

The website gets an SDK landing page, an API reference page per area,
a Rust SDK reference page per module, and a server-side search. The
pages run no script.

- The API reference is drawn at request time from the committed
  contracts: the app API (with Computers and Labs), the System One
  slice, and the decision API limited to the routes the public API
  forwards. Each operation shows its method, path, description,
  sign-in, parameters, request and response fields, grouped errors, a
  curl example, and the SDK functions that call it. Its operation ID
  is its anchor.
- The Rust SDK reference comes from docs/sdk/sdk-reference.json, which
  a syn-based test in openagents-sdk writes from the crate's source.
  The test fails when the file is stale or a public item has no doc
  comment.
- Fill the gaps: descriptions for the seven app operations that had
  none, and doc comments on every public SDK item.
- Link the SDK docs from /docs, /docs/api, and the sitemap.

Refs #12007.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep CoreAccount::close_clients for the identity's sign-in (#11995)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Drop the SDK's visitor module declaration; the identity retired the visitor flow (#11995)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Mark the website sign-in routes as this site's own (#12001)

The routes were missing from upstream::owned, so a request carrying the
session cookie was refused with 403 by the host guard (the poll after
sign-in) and, with --upstream, the routes would have been forwarded.
web_sign_in::owns now claims /login/ and /v1/web-sign-in/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read App Attest assertions and the development fixture correctly (#11994)

An assertion sets the attested-data flag but its authenticator data
stops after the counter, so the parser reads attested data only when it
is there. The real device fixture comes from a development build, so its
tests allow development keys, and a new test checks that a verifier for
production refuses it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Refuse wallet restore words that differ from the account's (#11995)

On a phone with an identity, the wallet's Restore from words now takes
only the identity's own words. Other words would split the wallet from
the account, so the screen says: "These words don't match your account.
To use different words, restore your account from them in Settings."
The account's Restore from 12 words is the one path that changes the
words; a wallet made after it takes them. A locked identity item
restores nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make a new wallet from the identity's 12 words (#11995, #11999)

"Make a wallet" made its own 12 words, so a person ended up with two
backups. A new wallet now takes the identity's words instead.

- `seed::create_with` makes the wallet's seed from the identity's
  entropy when the phone has an identity, and new words only when it has
  none (the identity then adopts the wallet's words when it is made). A
  locked identity item makes no wallet. The seed is still only added
  where none is stored, and the identity's item is only read.
- `CoreWallet::new` reads the phone's identity item through
  `openagents_account::identity::phone_entropy`; `Wallet::with_identity`
  takes any source, for tests.
- An existing wallet seed stays as it is and remains the source of the
  identity's words.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read the website sign-in waits from the app config (#12001)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Pass the loaded identity by reference in the phone's backup calls (#11995)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the phone's computer-code check in the sync crate instead of linking coder-computers (#12000)

coder-computers pulls coder-ui and rust-native's syntax highlighting,
whose tree-sitter clashes with the app workspace's pinned one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Import Arc in the Connect your phone sheet (#11998)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Hand the desktop's link offer to its engine process through the data dir (#12000)

The desktop engine runs as its own background service, so the in-process
link watch can't reach it. The window now also writes its offer to
openagents-account/identity/link-offer.json (mode 0600): the key, the
Keychain service that holds it, and a timestamp it refreshes every
minute. The secret never goes to disk. The engine polls that file, reads
the identity from the same Keychain item when the key matches (backing
off 30 seconds after a failed read), and writes "signed" and "linked"
to link-state.json beside it, which the window reads each second. The
in-process path stays for tests and a single-process app.

Also add a test that a website sign-in (#12001) by a key with no account
goes through #11994's new-key gate, and that a key with its account
signs the browser in without it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Tell the computer when its account link landed, and wire the desktop's signer (#12000)

After the phone's POST /v1/device/keys succeeds, it calls the new app
method AccountLinked {pubkey} over the device channel. The computer's
signer accepts it only from the grant it signed a proof for, once, and
the engine then calls link::linked, a new step in the desktop identity's
link watch (LinkState::Linked). The desktop signs in on Linked instead of
after a fixed wait; if no word comes within a minute it offers its key
again rather than signing in, since an unlinked key that signs in makes
its own account.

The engine follows link::watch for its data directory after the device
connection starts: while a key is offered it signs with that key (and
the deployment's key-link address from CODER_DESKTOP_API_URL), keeps the
signer through Signed, and clears it otherwise. link_account calls
link::signed after it signs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Connect a computer by scanning its code, and sign it in as the same person (#12000)

The phone scans a computer's connect code (or opens its connect link, or
takes a pasted code) and pairs with no prior registry entry: the computer
appears in Devices from the pairing alone. The host-signed grant and the
phone's key for that computer are kept in the Keychain
(`KeychainPairings`), so the pairing outlives the app, and the client
reconnects to saved computers on launch. Forgetting a pairing removes it.

The same scan links the computer to the phone's account, as NIP-HOST
"Account key link by QR" describes: the phone gets a key-link challenge
for its account, asks the computer over the new device connection to sign
a NIP-98 proof (app method `LinkAccount`), checks it, and posts it to
`POST /v1/device/keys` with its own session. The computer's signer
(`account_link::Signer`, wired through `Hosted::set_account_signer`)
answers only a fresh connect-code grant, once, for our key-link
addresses only.

The scanner also takes website sign-in codes (#12001): it names the
browser, asks first, and approves with the phone's identity key. The
website's app-site association now lists `/login/scan`.

Swift adds only the AVFoundation scanner, its result alerts, a Settings
row, the tutorial's scan button, and the universal-link handler.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sign in on the website with a phone scan or a browser extension (#12001)

/login now shows a QR code the OpenAgents phone app scans and approves
with its Nostr key, and a button for a NIP-07 browser extension. Both end
in the usual oa_cloud_session cookie, so /device (Coder 1.0's approval
page), /oauth/authorize, and Settings work for an account that has only
a key. GitHub sign-in stays for existing accounts.

- openagents-web: web_sign_in module. POST /login/key starts a sign-in
  (a challenge from the account service, a request held in memory for
  its five minutes, and an HttpOnly cookie that ties it to the browser);
  GET /login/key/{request}/qr.svg is the code; GET /v1/web-sign-in/{id}
  tells the phone which browser it signs in; POST /v1/web-sign-in/approve
  takes the phone's NIP-98 approval, checks it signs this request's
  challenge, and forwards it byte for byte to POST /v1/sessions/nostr;
  GET /login/key/{request}/status hands the session to the browser once.
  POST /login/key/extension signs a browser in from an extension.
  static/sign-in.js drives the page; no TypeScript.
- oa-auth: /v1/web-sign-in/approve and /login/key/extension join the
  sign-in paths, and a sign-in signed for them gets a browser session
  (book.issue), not an app session, so it isn't listed as a computer.
- openagents-sdk: ScannedLogin::parse, Client::scanned_login and
  Client::approve_scanned_login for the phone's scanner (#12000).
- Tests: the scan flow end to end with a throwaway key, including a
  key-only account approving a Coder device code; the extension flow;
  cross-site refusals; replay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add the desktop identity: welcome, silent sign-in, identity row (#11997)

Nobody signs in on the desktop. A fresh computer opens a welcome with
Connect your phone, Start here, or Restore from 12 words. After that the
identity's key signs in silently on every launch and renews before the
session ends, so configure_sync gets its bearer from the minted session.

- openagents_account::desktop::identity: the DesktopIdentity trait and
  KeyIdentity, which runs it over the shared Identities and the
  controller's key sign-in (#11995). A fresh computer makes no key and
  signs in with none until Start here or Restore. A computer signed in by
  an earlier build gets a key that joins that account. Also the welcome
  rules, typed-word checks, the short npub, the backup steps, and the
  words, with oa-copy tests.
- Connect your phone makes the key without signing in and offers it in
  desktop::identity::link for the device connection to sign a phone's
  link proof with (#12000). A marker on disk keeps a relaunch from signing
  in with the waiting key, since an unlinked key that signs in makes its
  own account (identity_taken). Once the proof is signed the key signs in
  as the phone's account.
- The sidebar row is an identity row: the short npub, a backup dot, and
  a menu with Your ID (copy), Linked devices, Back up your account (words
  behind a warning), Connect your phone, and Agent Lab. The browser
  sign-in, device code, and Sign out are gone; sign_in opens the welcome.
- The welcome and Back up are shell overlays; an identity-capture example
  draws every state headless.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show a Connect your phone QR code and run the device connection by default

The desktop app's NIP-HOST host now starts by default with an iroh
endpoint, signed in or not; OPENAGENTS_NIP_HOST=0 turns it off. Without
an account the host skips device-key registration instead of failing,
and a start or registration failure no longer stops the app.

A new Connect your phone sheet shows the host's connect link as a QR
code drawn on this computer. It asks for a new single-use code every
60 seconds, cancels the replaced code 60 seconds later, and cancels
every code it holds when it closes, when the window loses focus, or
after ten idle minutes. The copy action copies the text form and clears
it from the clipboard after 60 seconds. The sheet opens from the account
menu, a signed-out sidebar button, and Settings > Devices.

The engine serves CreateConnectCode and CancelConnectCodes only on the
in-process and localhost transports, never through the relay host or
the paired-device RPC. coder-host gains a ConnectCodes handle that the
control socket's invite now shares. The ConnectCode payload carries an
empty account_link field for the account-link request in #12000.

Refs #11998

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show a sign-up proof on a new key's first sign-in (#11995, #11994)

A new key's first sign-in now carries what the account service asks
for: an App Attest attestation over the challenge on the phone, or a
proof of work everywhere else.

- SDK: `key_challenge` and `sign_in_with_key_on` sign in over a given
  challenge with extra body fields, kept under `KEY_BODY_MAX` (16 KB).
  `solve_pow` solves `SHA-256(challenge ":" counter)` to `POW_BITS` (20)
  leading zero bits. The SDK now knows the sign-up refusal codes.
- `Controller` tries the plain key sign-in first, so a known key never
  pays for a proof. On `proof_required` it takes a fresh challenge and
  makes the proof off the async threads: App Attest when an `Attester`
  is set, otherwise or after `invalid_attestation`, a proof of work.
- Phone: `CoreAccount::set_app_attester` takes a Swift `AppAttester`.
  `AppAttest.swift` makes or reuses this install's App Attest key (its
  id kept in the Keychain, this device only) and attests it over
  `SHA-256(challenge)`, answering nil in the simulator so the core falls
  back to a proof of work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make the identity from 12 words and sign in silently with its key (#11995)

The phone and desktop core now give every device an identity on first
launch and sign in with it, with nothing for the person to do.

- Add `openagents_account::identity`: an `Identity` from 12 or 24 BIP-39
  words with its NIP-06 key, npub, nsec, and NIP-98 signing (it implements
  the SDK's `NostrSigner`). `Identities` opens the words from the
  identity's own Keychain item, or reuses the earlier app's wallet seed
  (`com.openagents.app.spark` / `seed-v1`, read only) as the words, and
  makes new words only when both are certainly absent. The item is on this
  device only by default, with an iCloud Keychain copy as a setting. It
  also holds restore from words, the backup check, and the words-saved
  record.
- Add silent sign-in to `Controller`: `start_with_key` reuses a saved
  session, adds the key to that session's account first when the device
  was signed in before the identity existed (`link_key`), and otherwise
  signs in with the key. `renew_with_key` signs in again before the
  session ends and swaps the session in place. `sign_in_with_key` serves
  restore from words.
- Phone FFI: `start_identity(device_name)`, `identity()` (npub, words
  saved, iCloud copy), `backup_words`, `backup_check`, `confirm_backup`,
  `restore_from_words`, `set_icloud_copy`, and `reveal_nsec`. The account
  timer renews with the key. The device-code `sign_in` is now available
  only to the account fixture's tests.
- Retire the visitor chat and its claim in the new app: the cloud chat is
  always an account chat, and its first send waits briefly for the silent
  sign-in. Remove the SDK's `visitor` module; the server routes stay.
- Add `desktop::identities` for the desktop's identity (UI in #11997).
- Require `NostrSigner: Send + Sync` so key sign-ins run on the shared
  runtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bound key-only accounts with App Attest, sign-up limits, and a breaker

A Nostr key costs nothing, so accounts that sign in with only a key get
limits that don't depend on GitHub or Apple (#11994):

- oa_auth::attest verifies App Attest attestations and assertions
  offline against the pinned Apple App Attestation Root CA: the x5c
  chain, the nonce extension, the key id, the app id
  (HQWSG26L43.com.openagents.app), the counter, and the AAGUID. A book
  beside the registry binds each attested key to one account. Tests use
  a real device's attestation and assertion (BSD-3-Clause fixture from
  github.com/bas-d/appattest).
- The Nostr sign-in takes a NewKeyGate that runs before a new key makes
  its account. The gateway's gate (gateway::key_accounts) accepts an
  `app_attest` attestation over the challenge, or a `pow` proof of work
  over it under per-address, per-/24, and global daily caps, reusing the
  agent self-registration helpers. Replayed sign-ins count toward no cap.
- Every key-only account that hasn't connected an account or paid shares
  one daily breaker on its free model allowance ($20 by default).
- GET /v1/account adds `account.free_cloud` (full, attested, none). The
  website sends `X-OpenAgents-Allowance: free-attested` for an attested
  key account, and the Computers service enrolls it in a smaller tier
  (40,000,000 CPU ms, migration 0018) that only moves up to the full $3.

Existing accounts and Coder 1.0.0 are unaffected: the new field and
header value are additive, and any non-key sign-in keeps the full
allowances.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Remove Sign in with Apple and stop GitHub sign-in from making accounts (#12005)

Sign in with Apple is removed everywhere:
- Server: POST /v1/sessions/apple (gateway and the oa-auth local
  service) and POST /v1/device/apple (web) answer 410 apple_removed,
  "Sign in with Apple has been removed." oa_auth::apple, its test keys,
  AuthError::AppleDenied, the gateway's accounts.apple config, and the
  staging/production render of it are gone. tenancy keeps the apple
  identity book and the apple: principal so linked accounts keep their
  data; only the find-or-create sign-in is removed.
- SDK: Client::sign_in_with_apple, AppleSignIn, and Error::AppleDenied
  are removed.

Bring the Spark wallet back to the phone and keep the old seed

The earlier OpenAgents app kept its Spark wallet seed in the Keychain item
com.openagents.app.spark / seed-v1. The current app has the same bundle ID
and team, so it now reads that item and opens the same wallet.

- apps/openagents/crates/mobile links crates/spark-wallet and turns on
  Breez's SQLite store there only; the app workspace patches boltz-client
  from the root's vendor/ copy, as the root workspace does.
- wallet::seed holds the seed rules. The KeyStore foreign trait can only
  read and add, so a stored seed can't be deleted or replaced. A read that
  fails for any reason but "not found" (a locked phone) shows an error and
  Try again, and never makes a seed. A seed is made only when the person
  taps Make a wallet after the store said none exists; Restore from 12 or
  24 words is offered only then too.
- wallet_seed_words returns the stored seed's words for the identity
  (#11995) and never writes.
- The Wallet screen is a Rust Native view: balance, Receive (Spark
  address, Lightning invoice, Bitcoin address, with QR), Send with a
  confirmed quote, Activity, the trust note, and Back up. The iOS shell
  adds the Keychain glue, the page, Face ID before the words, a
  capture-proof words sheet, and a 60-second local-only pasteboard copy.
  Wallet opens from the drawer toolbar, Settings, and -route wallet.
- An offline fixture wallet (-wallet-fixture, simulator and tests only)
  holds no money and never touches the Keychain.

Ported from the removed app (c63b8bbe5c^): DeviceKey.swift, WalletTab.swift,
and crates/openagents-mobile/src/wallet.rs, reduced to the main surface.
